page: Amazon Web Services i3en.large is a storage-optimized server instance designed for workloads requiring high local NVMe storage capacity. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 2 vCPUs (1 physical core with 2 threads) running at 3.1 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes a dedicated local storage allocation of 1250 GB NVMe SSD and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance is optimized primarily for storage density rather than raw compute power. The CPU performance is positioned in the lower tiers, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks scoring 1318.68 (weak) and 1731.97 (poor) respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 13.72 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 11.8 GB/sec for large block write operations, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked systems. Network performance is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3en.large offers a high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option where storage capacity is prioritized over processing speed. The primary trade-off is the weak CPU and memory performance, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 690.78 and a static web serving throughput of 1.87 GB/sec. This hardware profile is best suited for workloads such as localized databases, data caching, and storage-heavy applications that do not require intensive CPU processing.
